newsitem.title: USA: Network Peripherals has no comment on market rumor.
newsitem.headline: Network Peripherals has no comment on market rumor.

text.p: Network Peripherals Inc declined comment on market rumors that it would be bought out soon or that it had been issuing guidance that earnings would be nearly double Wall Street estimates for the full-year 1997.

Dane Iverson, manager of investor relations, said he was aware of market rumors of an imminent takeover deal or that the company's 1997 earnings would hit $0.80 a share, but said the company's policy is not to comment on market rumors.
"We'd like to direct people to the (earnings per share) estimate on the street, which is 45 cents a share, and let people evaluate the rumour based on that," he said.

Shares of Network Peripherals jumped to a 52-week high of 20-1/2 and closed at 19-3/4, up 1-1/4 in volume of more than one million shares. Earlier, traders cited rumors that the company would soon be subject to a bid of $38 from an unnamed suitor.
Iverson said the company does not comment on market rumors or takeover speculation, but added that such talk had persisted over a longer period of time involving the company.

"The policy is we don't comment on rumors," he said. "We've heard buyout rumours all the time, we can't comment specificially on it. These things happen all the time. We've heard buyout rumors for long periods of time."
On the rumor the company was issuing guidance that its earnings would be roughly double Wall Street's estimates, Iverson said: "We never ever tell people a specific number coming forward."
Nevertheless, he pointed to the current Wall Street consensus estimate for 1997 as compiled by First Call."Our
key is to keep executing," he said. ((--sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau +1 415 846 5400))
